newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta treasurer says leaving for own reasons.
newsitem.headline: Alberta treasurer says leaving for own reasons.

text.p: Alberta treasurer Jim Dinning, who announced on Thursday he was leaving politics when his current term ends, said he made the decision for personal reasons.

"I came to this conclusion on and off for the last number of months," Dinning told reporters after a speech to Calgary business audience. "This is a personal decision that's right for Jim Dinning in 1996. I leave with a tremendous sense of accomplishment behind me."
Dinning, who has been a member of Alberta's ruling Conservative government representing a Calgary district since 1986, had been touted has a possible successor to current Premier Ralph Klein.
He has been the oil-rich province's treasurer since 1992.

Dinning, who has been called an architect of Alberta's economic recovery over the last four years, brought down two annual surplus budgets after a series of deep government cutbacks and reorganizations.
He said he had no current job offers from the private sector. Dinning worked in the oil industry before entering politics.
High oil prices and a strong economy are expected to allow Dinning to leave politics after forecasting another major budget surplus in 1997.
